q: 办公室里___三台电脑。
py: bàn gōng shì lǐ yǒu sān tái diàn nǎo
en: There are three computers in the office.
why: New, counted things at a place: Place + 有 + number + measure + noun. 在 would need the computers first (电脑在办公室里), and 着 needs a posture or placement verb before it.

q: 我的杯子___桌子上。
py: wǒ de bēi zi zài zhuō zi shàng
en: My cup is on the table.
why: 我的杯子 is a known thing, so it comes first and 在 says where it is. 有 introduces something new and 是 does not locate an object like this.

q: 医院旁边___一家药店。
py: yī yuàn páng biān yǒu yī jiā yào diàn
en: There is a pharmacy next to the hospital.
why: The place opens the sentence and an indefinite thing (一家药店) follows 有. 在 would need the pharmacy first, and 着 cannot attach to a bare place phrase.

q: 经理___办公室里。
py: jīng lǐ zài bàn gōng shì lǐ
en: The manager is in the office.
why: A known person located somewhere takes 在: Person + 在 + Place. 有 and 是 cannot link a person to the room they are in.

q: 冰箱里___水果。
py: bīng xiāng lǐ méi yǒu shuǐ guǒ
en: There is no fruit in the fridge.
why: 有 is only ever negated with 没, so the positive 有 becomes 没有. 不有 does not exist, and 不在 is for a known thing that is not at a place.

q: 王经理___办公室。
py: wáng jīng lǐ bù zài bàn gōng shì
en: Manager Wang is not in the office.
why: The positive version is 王经理在办公室, so the negative is 不在. 没有 would say he has no office, and 不是 would say he is not the office.

q: 药在桌子___。
py: yào zài zhuō zi shàng
en: The medicine is on the table.
why: A table is an object, not a place, so it needs 上 for its surface. Leaving it off (在桌子) is incomplete, and 里 would put the medicine inside the table.

q: 水在杯子___。
py: shuǐ zài bēi zi lǐ
en: The water is in the cup.
why: Liquid inside a container needs 里 after the noun. A bare 在杯子 is incomplete and 杯子上 would mean on the surface of the cup.

q: 他在北京___工作。
py: tā zài běi jīng gōng zuò
en: He works in Beijing.
why: City names are already places, so nothing follows 北京. Adding 里 or 上 is the classic English-prepositions mistake.

q: 药店在医院___。
py: yào diàn zài yī yuàn duì miàn
en: The pharmacy is across from the hospital.
why: The cue says across from, which is 对面. 旁边 means right beside, and 中间 needs two things to be between.

q: 我们公司对面___那家医院。
zh: 我们公司对面是那家医院。
py: wǒ men gōng sī duì miàn shì nà jiā yī yuàn
en: Across from our company is that hospital.
why: With the place first and a definite thing (那家医院) named after it, the verb is 是. 在 needs the thing before it and the place after it.

q: 我旁边___小王，他是新来的同事。
zh: 我旁边是小王，他是新来的同事。
py: wǒ páng biān shì xiǎo wáng, tā shì xīn lái de tóng shì
en: The person next to me is Xiao Wang, a new colleague.
why: Place first, then naming who is there: 是. 在 would put the place after the verb and cannot follow 我旁边.

q: 他的桌子上___是文件，一点空地方都没有。
zh: 他的桌子上都是文件，一点空地方都没有。
py: tā de zhuō zi shàng dōu shì wén jiàn, yī diǎn kòng dì fang dōu méi yǒu
en: His desk is covered in documents; there is no free space at all.
why: 都是 after a place means it is full of one kind of thing. 也 means also and 才 means only then, neither fits a desk covered in documents.

q: 墙上___一张公司地图。
zh: 墙上挂着一张公司地图。
py: qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng gōng sī dì tú
en: A map of the company is hanging on the wall.
why: Place + V着 + number + measure + noun describes how something is placed. 挂过 would mean it once hung there, and 在挂 is not this pattern.

q: 门口站___一个人。
py: mén kǒu zhàn zhe yī gè rén
en: There is someone standing at the door.
why: 站着 describes the state of standing, with the new person after the verb. 过 means it happened before, and 站在 would need a place after it.

q: 医生的桌子上放___一台电脑和两本书。
zh: 医生的桌子上放着一台电脑和两本书。
py: yī shēng de zhuō zi shàng fàng zhe yī tái diàn nǎo hé liǎng běn shū
en: There is a computer and two books on the doctor's desk.
why: The desk is the place, so 放着 describes what lies there. 放在 and 放到 need the place after the verb, but the place is already at the start.

q: 昨天我们公司来___一位新同事。
zh: 昨天我们公司来了一位新同事。
py: zuó tiān wǒ men gōng sī lái le yī wèi xīn tóng shì
en: A new colleague came to our company yesterday.
why: A newcomer after 来 takes 了: Place + 来了 + number + measure + noun. 着 describes a continuing state, not an arrival, and 在 does not belong after 来.

q: 我们部门___了一个新经理。
zh: 我们部门来了一个新经理。
py: wǒ men bù mén lái le yī gè xīn jīng lǐ
en: A new manager has joined our department.
why: 来 is the verb of arrival, so the new manager joined. 走 would say a manager left, and 站 is a posture verb that does not fit 了 here.

q: 上个月我们大楼里搬___了一家公司。
zh: 上个月我们大楼里搬来了一家公司。
py: shàng gè yuè wǒ men dà lóu lǐ bān lái le yī jiā gōng sī
en: A company moved into our building last month.
why: 搬来 means move in, with the new company after 了. 搬走 would mean one left, and 搬开 means move aside.

q: 我们公司附近___很多饭馆，午饭很方便。
zh: 我们公司附近有很多饭馆，午饭很方便。
py: wǒ men gōng sī fù jìn yǒu hěn duō fàn guǎn, wǔ fàn hěn fāng biàn
en: There are a lot of restaurants near our company, so lunch is easy.
why: 很多饭馆 is indefinite, so the place comes first and 有 follows. 在 would need the restaurants first, and 着 needs a placement verb.

q: 我的包里___一瓶药和一些水。
zh: 我的包里有一瓶药和一些水。
py: wǒ de bāo lǐ yǒu yī píng yào hé yī xiē shuǐ
en: There is a bottle of medicine and some water in my bag.
why: Listing new things in a place: Place + 有 + things. 没有 contradicts the cue, and 着 needs a verb like 放 in front of it.

q: 会议室里___十几个人，大家都在等经理。
zh: 会议室里有十几个人，大家都在等经理。
py: huì yì shì lǐ yǒu shí jǐ gè rén, dà jiā dōu zài děng jīng lǐ
en: There are a dozen or so people in the meeting room, all waiting for the manager.
why: 十几个人 is an indefinite number of people, so Place + 有 + number + measure + noun. 在 would put the people first as the subject.

q: 你要的那份文件___我的电脑里。
zh: 你要的那份文件在我的电脑里。
py: nǐ yào de nà fèn wén jiàn zài wǒ de diàn nǎo lǐ
en: The file you want is on my computer.
why: 那份文件 is a specific, known file, so it comes first and 在 gives its location. 有 would present it as something new, and 是 does not locate it.

q: 请问，药店___哪儿？
py: qǐng wèn, yào diàn zài nǎ r
en: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?
why: Asking where a known place is takes Thing + 在 + 哪儿. 有 cannot be followed by 哪儿 in this question, and 着 is not a verb here.

q: 今天上午李老师___办公室，你下午再来吧。
zh: 今天上午李老师不在办公室，你下午再来吧。
py: jīn tiān shàng wǔ lǐ lǎo shī bù zài bàn gōng shì, nǐ xià wǔ zài lái ba
en: Teacher Li is not in the office this morning, so come back this afternoon.
why: The positive is 李老师在办公室, so the negative is 不在. 没有 would say he has no office at all, which does not fit the follow-up clause.

q: 我的钱包里___钱，只有几张卡。
zh: 我的钱包里没有钱，只有几张卡。
py: wǒ de qián bāo lǐ méi yǒu qián, zhǐ yǒu jǐ zhāng kǎ
en: There is no cash in my wallet, only a few cards.
why: The positive is 钱包里有钱, so the negative is 没有. 不有 does not exist, and 不在 is for a known thing missing from a place.

q: 你要的药___抽屉里，再找找别的地方吧。
zh: 你要的药不在抽屉里，再找找别的地方吧。
py: nǐ yào de yào bù zài chōu tì lǐ, zài zhǎo zhao bié de dì fang ba
en: The medicine you want is not in the drawer, so look somewhere else.
why: 你要的药 is a specific, known thing, so the positive uses 在 and the negative is 不在. 没有 cannot take 抽屉里 as its object here.

q: 那张照片挂在墙___。
py: nà zhāng zhào piàn guà zài qiáng shàng
en: That photo is hung on the wall.
why: A wall is a surface, so it takes 上. Without it 墙 is not yet a place, and 里 would mean inside the wall.

q: 你的药在我的包___。
py: nǐ de yào zài wǒ de bāo lǐ
en: Your medicine is in my bag.
why: Something inside a bag needs 里 after 包. 上 would put it on top of the bag, and a bare 在我的包 is incomplete.

q: 我姐姐在上海___当医生。
py: wǒ jiě jie zài shàng hǎi dāng yī shēng
en: My older sister works as a doctor in Shanghai.
why: 上海 is a city, already a place, so no 里 or 上 follows it. Adding either is the English-preposition mistake.

q: 他在公司的电梯___遇到了经理。
zh: 他在公司的电梯里遇到了经理。
py: tā zài gōng sī de diàn tī lǐ yù dào le jīng lǐ
en: He ran into the manager in the company lift.
why: The lift is an enclosed space, so it needs 里 to become a place for 'in the lift'. 外 would put the meeting outside it, and the learner's tempting 上 is also heard, so it is not offered.

q: 药店在我们公司___，走路五分钟就到。
zh: 药店在我们公司旁边，走路五分钟就到。
py: yào diàn zài wǒ men gōng sī páng biān, zǒu lù wǔ fēn zhōng jiù dào
en: The pharmacy is right next to our company, five minutes on foot.
why: The cue says next to, which is 旁边. 对面 means across the way, and 中间 needs two reference points.

q: 小王坐在我___。
py: xiǎo wáng zuò zài wǒ hòu miàn
en: Xiao Wang sits behind me.
why: The location word comes after the reference noun (我后面). Behind is 后面; 前面 means in front, and 对面 means opposite.

q: 我们的办公室在电梯和楼梯___，很容易找。
zh: 我们的办公室在电梯和楼梯中间，很容易找。
py: wǒ men de bàn gōng shì zài diàn tī hé lóu tī zhōng jiān, hěn róng yì zhǎo
en: Our office is between the lift and the stairs, so it is easy to find.
why: Between two things is 中间 after both nouns. 旁边 means beside one thing, and 里面 means inside.

q: 办公室的抽屉里___很多药，有感冒药，也有胃药。
zh: 办公室的抽屉里有很多药，有感冒药，也有胃药。
py: bàn gōng shì de chōu tì lǐ yǒu hěn duō yào, yǒu gǎn mào yào, yě yǒu wèi yào
en: There is a lot of medicine in the office drawer, both cold medicine and stomach medicine.
why: 很多药 is new and indefinite, so Place + 有 + noun. 在 would need the medicine first, and 着 needs a placement verb.

q: 你要找的王医生___三楼的办公室，不在一楼。
zh: 你要找的王医生在三楼的办公室，不在一楼。
py: nǐ yào zhǎo de wáng yī shēng zài sān lóu de bàn gōng shì, bù zài yī lóu
en: Dr Wang, whom you are looking for, is in the third-floor office, not on the first floor.
why: Dr Wang is a known person located by 在, which also matches the contrast with 不在一楼. 有 would introduce him as new, and 是 would equate him with an office.

q: 我们办公室的左边是会议室，右边___经理的办公室。
zh: 我们办公室的左边是会议室，右边是经理的办公室。
py: wǒ men bàn gōng shì de zuǒ biān shì huì yì shì, yòu biān shì jīng lǐ de bàn gōng shì
en: To the left of our office is the meeting room, to the right the manager's office.
why: Both halves name what occupies a spot, so 是 repeats. 在 would need the manager's office first and the place after.

q: 那支笔在他的口袋___。
py: nà zhī bǐ zài tā de kǒu dài lǐ
en: That pen is in his pocket.
why: Inside a pocket needs 里 after 口袋. 上 would put the pen on the outside of the pocket, and 外 would put it outside the pocket altogether.

q: 医院___有一家很大的药店，买药很方便。
zh: 医院外面有一家很大的药店，买药很方便。
py: yī yuàn wài miàn yǒu yī jiā hěn dà de yào diàn, mǎi yào hěn fāng biàn
en: There is a big pharmacy outside the hospital, so buying medicine is easy.
why: The cue says outside, which is 外面 placed after 医院. 里面 means inside, and 后面 means behind.

q: 这个办公室里___空调。
zh: 这个办公室里没有空调。
py: zhè gè bàn gōng shì lǐ méi yǒu kōng tiáo
en: There is no air conditioner in this office.
why: The positive is 办公室里有空调, so the negative is 没有 with a bare noun. 不有 does not exist, and 不在 is for a known thing.

zh: 办公室里有一台打印机。
py: bàn gōng shì lǐ yǒu yī tái dǎ yìn jī
en: There is a printer in the office.
why: Place first, then 有, then the new thing with its measure word. The printer cannot open the sentence.

py: wǒ de yào zài bāo lǐ
en: My medicine is in my bag.
why: A known thing (我的药) goes first and 在 links it to the place. 包里 has 里 because a bag is an object.

zh: 公司后面有一个停车场。
py: gōng sī hòu miàn yǒu yī gè tíng chē chǎng
en: There is a car park behind the company.
why: The location word follows the noun: 公司后面. That place opens the sentence, and 有 introduces the car park.

py: xiǎo wáng bù zài gōng sī
en: Xiao Wang is not at the company.
why: The positive is 小王在公司, so the negative is 不在. 公司 needs no 里 here.

py: bàn gōng shì lǐ méi yǒu rén le
en: There is nobody in the office any more.
why: Place + 没有 + bare noun, and 了 at the end marks the change. The noun has no number or measure word.

py: mén kǒu zhàn zhe yī wèi yī shēng
en: A doctor is standing at the door.
why: Place first, then 站着, then the new person with a measure word. The doctor cannot come before the verb.

zh: 我们部门来了一个新同事。
py: wǒ men bù mén lái le yī gè xīn tóng shì
en: A new colleague has joined our department.
why: The place opens the sentence and the newcomer follows 来了. Ending with the department, as in English, is wrong.

py: nǐ de yǎn jìng zài yǐ zi xià miàn
en: Your glasses are under the chair.
why: A known thing goes first and 在 links it to the place. The location word 下面 follows 椅子.

py: yín háng páng biān shì wǒ men gōng sī
en: Next to the bank is our company.
why: 我们公司 is a definite occupant named after the place, so the verb is 是. 有 could not introduce it, and 在 would not follow the place.

zh: 昨天我们公司来了两位新同事。
py: zuó tiān wǒ men gōng sī lái le liǎng wèi xīn tóng shì
en: Two new colleagues came to our company yesterday.
why: The time and place come first (either order), and the newcomers follow 来了. Putting the place last is the English order.

zh: 会议室里坐着十几个开会的人。
py: huì yì shì lǐ zuò zhe shí jǐ gè kāi huì de rén
en: A dozen or so people are sitting in the meeting room, in a meeting.
why: Place + V着 + number + measure + modified noun. The new people are described after the verb, not before it.

py: qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng rén tǐ tú
en: A diagram of the human body hangs on the wall.
why: Place first, then 挂着, then the new thing with its measure word 张. 墙上 has 上 because a wall is a surface.

zh: 药店在银行和医院中间。
py: yào diàn zài yín háng hé yī yuàn zhōng jiān
en: The pharmacy is between the bank and the hospital.
why: 中间 follows the two reference nouns joined by 和. The two nouns may swap places, but 中间 cannot come before them.

py: jīng lǐ zhàn zài wǒ men qián miàn
en: The manager is standing in front of us.
why: The location word follows its noun: 我们前面, never 前面我们. 站在 puts the manager at that place.

zh: 我的手机不在桌子上，也不在包里。
py: wǒ de shǒu jī bù zài zhuō zi shàng, yě bù zài bāo lǐ
en: My phone is not on the table, and not in my bag either.
why: The phone is a known thing, so each part uses 不在 rather than 没有. 也不在 repeats the negative for the second place.

zh: 我们公司附近一家药店也没有。
py: wǒ men gōng sī fù jìn yī jiā yào diàn yě méi yǒu
en: There is not a single pharmacy near our company.
why: 一 + measure + noun + 也没有 stresses that there is not even one. 也 goes directly before 没有.

py: zhuō zi shàng yǒu sān bēi kā fēi
en: There are three cups of coffee on the table.
why: Place first, 有, then the counted new thing. The coffee cannot come first because it is indefinite.

py: bí zi zài yǎn jing xià miàn
en: The nose is below the eyes.
why: 鼻子 is a known thing, so 在 links it to the place 眼睛下面. The location word follows its noun.

py: yī shēng zhàn zài bìng rén páng biān
en: The doctor is standing next to the patient.
why: 旁边 comes after 病人. 站在 gives the place after the verb, so the place phrase is not fronted.

zh: 他的脸上有一个小伤口。
py: tā de liǎn shàng yǒu yī gè xiǎo shāng kǒu
en: There is a small cut on his face.
why: Place first, then 有, then the new thing. The cut is indefinite, so it cannot open the sentence with 在.

py: yī yuàn lǐ lái le hěn duō bìng rén
en: A lot of patients have come to the hospital.
why: The newcomers (很多病人) go after 来了 with the place first. 病人来了医院里 is the English order.

zh: 上个月我们部门走了两位老同事。
py: shàng gè yuè wǒ men bù mén zǒu le liǎng wèi lǎo tóng shì
en: Two long-serving colleagues left our department last month.
why: Departures use the same pattern: place and time first, 走了, then the people who left. The time word can swap with the place.

py: mén kǒu tíng zhe yī liàng jiù hù chē
en: An ambulance is parked at the entrance.
why: Place + 停着 + number + measure + noun. 辆 is the measure word for vehicles, and the ambulance follows the verb.

zh: 我们公司对面都是医院。
py: wǒ men gōng sī duì miàn dōu shì yī yuàn
en: Across from our company it is all hospitals.
why: 都是 after a place says it is full of one kind of thing. 有 would not carry the meaning that nothing else is there.

zh: 你要的那份文件在经理的桌子上。
py: nǐ yào de nà fèn wén jiàn zài jīng lǐ de zhuō zi shàng
en: The file you want is on the manager's desk.
why: The definite file goes first, then 在, then the place. 桌子上 has 上 because a desk is a surface.

py: zhuō zi shàng yī fèn wén jiàn yě méi yǒu
en: There is not a single document on the table.
why: To stress not even one, put 一份文件 in front of 也没有. Plain 没有 takes a bare noun (没有文件); the counted noun before 也没有 is what gives 'not a single one'.

src_py: wǒ de shǒu jī zài zhuō zi shàng
task: Say there is a phone on the table (not mine).
py: zhuō zi shàng yǒu yī bù shǒu jī
en: There is a phone on the table.
why: An unknown phone is introduced after 有 with the place first. 在 is for the known 我的手机.

src_py: gōng sī páng biān yǒu yī jiā yī yuàn
task: Use 是 to say what is next to the company.
py: gōng sī páng biān shì yī jiā yī yuàn
en: Next to the company is a hospital.
why: 是 identifies what occupies the spot, replacing 有 in the same frame.

src: 办公室门口有一个病人。
src_py: bàn gōng shì mén kǒu yǒu yī gè bìng rén
task: Say the patient is sitting there.
zh: 办公室门口坐着一个病人。
py: bàn gōng shì mén kǒu zuò zhe yī gè bìng rén
en: A patient is sitting at the office door.
why: 坐着 replaces 有 to show the posture. The patient stays after the verb.

src: 昨天办公室来了一位客人。
src_py: zuó tiān bàn gōng shì lái le yī wèi kè rén
task: Change the time to this morning (今天上午).
zh: 今天上午办公室来了一位客人。
py: jīn tiān shàng wǔ bàn gōng shì lái le yī wèi kè rén
en: A guest came to the office this morning.
why: Only the time word changes. The newcomer stays after 来了, and the time and place can swap.

task: Say it is in the drawer (抽屉).
py: yào zài chōu tì lǐ
en: The medicine is in the drawer.
why: A drawer is a container, so it needs 里 rather than 上.

src: 你要的文件在我的电脑里。
src_py: nǐ yào de wén jiàn zài wǒ de diàn nǎo lǐ
zh: 你要的文件不在我的电脑里。
py: nǐ yào de wén jiàn bù zài wǒ de diàn nǎo lǐ
en: The file you want is not on my computer.
why: A known file located with 在 is negated with 不在. 没有 does not fit a definite thing.

src_py: yào diàn zài yín háng páng biān
task: Say it is across from the bank.
py: yào diàn zài yín háng duì miàn
en: The pharmacy is across from the bank.
why: Swap 旁边 for 对面 and keep it after 银行.

src_py: bàn gōng shì lǐ yǒu liǎng gè rén
task: Say there are a lot of people.
py: bàn gōng shì lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén
en: There are a lot of people in the office.
why: 很多 replaces the number and measure, and the pattern stays Place + 有 + noun.

s_py: zhuō zi shàng zài yī tái diàn nǎo
py: zhuō zi shàng yǒu yī tái diàn nǎo
en: There is a computer on the table.
why: 在 cannot be the verb after a bare place with a new thing. With the place first, an indefinite thing is introduced by 有.

s_py: xiǎo wáng yǒu huì yì shì lǐ
py: xiǎo wáng zài huì yì shì lǐ
en: Xiao Wang is in the meeting room.
why: Locating a person uses 在. 有 means to have or there is, and cannot link 小王 to a place.

s_py: yǎn jìng zài zhuō zi
py: yǎn jìng zài zhuō zi shàng
en: The glasses are on the table.
why: 桌子 is an object and needs 上 to become a place after 在.

s_py: wǒ gē ge zài shàng hǎi lǐ gōng zuò
py: wǒ gē ge zài shàng hǎi gōng zuò
en: My older brother works in Shanghai.
why: City names are already places, so 里 must not be added after them.

s_py: yín háng zài páng biān gōng sī
py: yín háng zài gōng sī páng biān
en: The bank is next to the company.
why: The location word comes after the reference noun: 公司旁边. The English order is wrong.

s_py: chōu tì lǐ bù yǒu yào
py: chōu tì lǐ méi yǒu yào
en: There is no medicine in the drawer.
why: 有 is only ever negated with 没, so 不有 never exists.

s_py: yī gè yī shēng zhàn zhe zài mén kǒu
py: mén kǒu zhàn zhe yī gè yī shēng
en: A doctor is standing at the door.
why: A new person is introduced after the verb, with the place first. 站着 is not followed by 在 and a place.

s: 昨天医院来着两位新医生。
s_py: zuó tiān yī yuàn lái zhe liǎng wèi xīn yī shēng
zh: 昨天医院来了两位新医生。
py: zuó tiān yī yuàn lái le liǎng wèi xīn yī shēng
en: Two new doctors came to the hospital yesterday.
why: An arrival is a completed event, so 来 takes 了. 着 describes a continuing state and cannot go after 来 here.

s: 我的朋友现在在中国里。
s_py: wǒ de péng you xiàn zài zài zhōng guó lǐ
py: wǒ de péng you xiàn zài zài zhōng guó
en: My friend is in China now.
why: Country names are already places. 里 must not follow 中国.

s_py: jīng lǐ zuò zài hòu miàn wǒ men
py: jīng lǐ zuò zài wǒ men hòu miàn
en: The manager sits behind us.
why: The location word follows the noun: 我们后面. Putting it first is the English order.

s_py: xué xiào duì miàn zài yī jiā yào diàn
py: xué xiào duì miàn shì yī jiā yào diàn
en: Across from the school is a pharmacy.
why: With the place at the start, the verb is 是 (or 有), never 在. 在 needs the thing before it.

s: 我家附近有一家很大的医院。
s_py: wǒ jiā fù jìn yǒu yī jiā hěn dà de yī yuàn
zh: 我家附近有一家很大的医院。
py: wǒ jiā fù jìn yǒu yī jiā hěn dà de yī yuàn
en: There is a very big hospital near my home.
why: Place first, 有, then an indefinite thing. The long description of the hospital does not change the pattern.

s_py: yī yuàn duì miàn shì wǒ men gōng sī
py: yī yuàn duì miàn shì wǒ men gōng sī
en: Across from the hospital is our company.
why: A definite occupant (我们公司) after a place takes 是. 有 would be wrong here, and 在 does not follow the place.

s_py: wǒ mā ma zài yī yuàn gōng zuò
py: wǒ mā ma zài yī yuàn gōng zuò
en: My mother works at the hospital.
why: 医院 is an institution that already counts as a place, so 里 or 上 is not needed after 在.

s: 他在飞机上看了一份文件。
s_py: tā zài fēi jī shàng kàn le yī fèn wén jiàn
zh: 他在飞机上看了一份文件。
py: tā zài fēi jī shàng kàn le yī fèn wén jiàn
en: He read a document on the plane.
why: Chinese uses 上 for vehicles where English says on or in. 在飞机上 is the standard form.

s_py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān bù zài gōng sī
py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān bù zài gōng sī
en: The manager was not at the company yesterday.
why: 不在 also works for a past day. A known person not at a place is always 不在, never 不有.

s_py: yào xiāng lǐ yī piàn yào yě méi yǒu
py: yào xiāng lǐ yī piàn yào yě méi yǒu
en: There is not a single pill in the medicine box.
why: 一 + measure + noun + 也没有 is the emphatic not even one. The number and measure only come before 也没有.

s_py: bìng chuáng shàng tǎng zhe yī wèi lǎo rén
py: bìng chuáng shàng tǎng zhe yī wèi lǎo rén
en: An old man is lying on the hospital bed.
why: Place + 躺着 + number + measure + noun is the standard way to describe who lies there. The old man follows the verb.

s: 经理等的客人已经来了。
s_py: jīng lǐ děng de kè rén yǐ jīng lái le
zh: 经理等的客人已经来了。
py: jīng lǐ děng de kè rén yǐ jīng lái le
en: The guest the manager was waiting for has arrived.
why: A definite, expected guest goes before the verb as the subject. Only a new, unexpected arrival goes after 来了.

s: 前面有一家药店，我去买点药。
s_py: qián miàn yǒu yī jiā yào diàn, wǒ qù mǎi diǎn yào
zh: 前面有一家药店，我去买点药。
py: qián miàn yǒu yī jiā yào diàn, wǒ qù mǎi diǎn yào
en: There is a pharmacy ahead, I will go and buy some medicine.
why: A location word can stand alone as the place. 前面 opens the sentence and 有 introduces the new pharmacy.
